read_before_generating: brief/MAP_closed.json (116 items; symmetry-relevant items quoted in each idea)
lens_level_findings: Every symmetry the programme uses is non-modular (FGHR invariant ring over F_p / F_{2^n}-valued coordinates; Faugere-Svartz blocks need |G| odd). Over F_2 the summand-permutation groups of the CHAINED presentations are 2-groups (Z/2 at m=2,3; D_4 at the balanced m=4 chain) and are therefore modular: no Reynolds operator, no character blocks. The programme has no tool for this case; MP-symmetry-5 supplies the first one (transfer vs fixed-point filtration).

The odd-order stabilisers that DO exist (C_n Frobenius on the free-shift barrel; Z/3 cyclic permutation on the unchained S_4 descent) give the refutation certificate 1 in W_c from the trivial-character block alone, over F_2, with no F_{2^130} arithmetic (MP-symmetry-1). Prototype (ideas/symmetry_proto_z3_block.py, n=7, l=3): closure degree 9 agrees on full (910x512, rank 509) and trivial block (910x176, rank 175); span invariance verified (rank 7 -> 7).

The group-algebra lift N1 and the mu_{2n+1} exponent-shift symmetry are the same object: F_2[Z/(2n+1)] = F_2 x F_{2^n} x F_{2^n} (verified in gp: X^23-1, X^47-1, X^263-1 split as (X-1) times two reciprocal irreducibles of degree n). The exact lift is the field identity plus a parity identity plus the identity on the 'shadow' x-bar = sum gamma^{-k}; for even gamma-weight summands the parity identity is identically false (S_3(0,0,e)=1 over F_2). N1 is a relabelling, not a non-generic route (MP-symmetry-3).

Twist-avoiding (all-lift) subspaces at prime degree are exactly the F_2-subspaces on which the component function Tr(beta/x) of the multiplicative inverse is affine (beta = sqrt(b)); the condition is invariant under the 2-torsion translation x -> beta/x. This connects open lever 7 to the Carlet / Carlet-Hou sum-freedom literature on the inverse function restricted to subspaces and to Kolomeets' component-constant-on-subspace results (MP-symmetry-4).

Galois cohomology of the factor-base torsor (task focus) reduces, over a finite field, to the connecting homomorphism E'(F_q) -> H^1(Gal, E[phi]) = Z/2 of the 2-isogeny E -> E/<T>: a homomorphic 1-bit filter, already closed by LEAD-ICB-cofactor-torsion-quotients and TREAT-transport-conservation. No idea filed; recorded as an obstruction note.

Nothing in this lens changes an exponent (TREAT-symmetry-inventory). The honest value is (i) making the undecided solving-degree cells cheaper by |G|^2 in memory for the UNSAT (certificate) side, (ii) a per-character organisation of the lever-1 proof route, (iii) two theory closures (N1, twist-avoiding) that remove items from future lists.

ideas.title: Trivial-character (Reynolds) Macaulay refutation for odd-order presentation stabilisers: certificate census for the (4,l) cells at 1/|G|^2 memory over F_2
ideas.statement: Let F be a Boolean presentation (in B = F_2[x]/(x^2-x)) of a point-decomposition instance that is invariant under a finite group G of ODD order acting by permuting variables: (i) the Frobenius cyclic group C_n on the barrel formulation with free target shift (summand i in sigma^{k_i}(W) with one-hot selectors, target sigma^j(x_R) with one-hot selector), (ii) the cyclic group Z/3 permuting the three summand coordinate blocks of the UNCHAINED Weil-descended S_4 with x_1,x_2,x_3 in one subspace V, (iii) their product C_n x Z/3 (order 3n, odd). Then for every c: 1 in W_c(F) if and only if 1 in R(W_c(F)), where R = sum_{g in G} g is the Reynolds operator (|G| is invertible in F_2) and R(W_c) is spanned by the orbit sums of the Macaulay rows, expressed in the basis of orbit sums of squarefree monomials (dimension ~ C(N,<=c)/|G|). The refutation degree c* = min{c : 1 in W_c}, i.e. the UNSAT side of the solving degree and every 'd_F >= 5' closure certificate, is therefore computable from a matrix with ~1/|G| rows and ~1/|G| columns over F_2, with no extension-field arithmetic (the F_{2^130} block of G2 is only needed to extract solutions). The reduction stacks with FGHR's 2-torsion frame (u = 1/(x+1), w = u^2+u are F_2-rational maps, so they commute with sigma and with the summand permutation).
ideas.mechanism: W_c is G-stable because the generator set is G-stable up to span (the components of a G-invariant F_{2^n}-valued polynomial are permuted in a normal basis, or their span is preserved in any basis) and the degree filtration is permutation-invariant. For |G| odd, R is a projector with image B^G and R(W_c) = W_c cap B^G; since 1 in B^G, 1 in W_c <=> 1 in R(W_c). Orbit sums of squarefree monomials form a basis of B_{<=c}^G (orbits have size 1 or |G| for prime |G|; size 1,3 for Z/3; 1,n for C_n; 1,3,n,3n for the product). Rows: R(m f_i) for monomial multiples m f_i with deg <= c; for G-stable generator spans one representative per row orbit suffices. The computation is a rank/membership test on a (rows/|G|) x (cols/|G|) F_2 matrix: memory /|G|^2, dense time /|G|^omega. Prototype at n=7, l=3 (Z/3, unchained S_4, K_0 model y^2+xy=x^3+1): components have Boolean degree 6; closure at c=9 on both; full 910x512 rank 509 vs trivial block 910x176 rank 175; AGREEMENT True. Second run n=11, l=4 (12 unknowns, 883 unsat targets available): closure at c=9 (< 3l = 12) on both; full 3289x4017 rank 3281 vs trivial block 3289x1349 rank 1125 (ratio 0.343); AGREEMENT True; 20 s total. The same code (ideas/symmetry_proto_z3_block.py, args n l seed cmax) runs the census.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-symmetry-inventory ('symmetry cannot change an exponent; it CAN make the decisive solving-degree cells affordable') - we accept the first clause and target the second. LEAD-ICB-frobenius-search-symmetry (closed_obstructed): 'Frobenius is an equivariance between conjugate instances, not a per-instance symmetry; equivariant elimination regressed 0.29-0.59x on production systems; Frobenius-equivariant F4 on the full barrel remains an open ENABLER'. LEAD-ICE-boolean-f4-f5-f6-engines (closed_dominated by the pair table).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: (a) The free-target-shift barrel is a genuine stabiliser of ONE instance (the instance 'does some conjugate sigma^j R decompose over the orbit-union base', which is relation-equivalent to R since log sigma^j R = mu^j log R and the base is sigma-stable), not a conjugation between instances; the Z/3 summand permutation is a genuine stabiliser of a fixed-target instance - exactly the 'genuine single-target stabilizer' the closure's scope_limits leave open. (b) The target is the certificate census (lever 1: UNSAT closure degrees at (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) and the d_F >= 5 population census), which is a measurement, not an oracle; the pair-table dominance that closed the engine lead is irrelevant to a measurement of d_F. (c) The 'regressed on production' finding concerned non-sigma-symmetric production systems; here the symmetric presentation is built on purpose. (d) The G2 scoping assumed both character blocks are needed (F_{2^130} arithmetic, c_mul penalty); for refutation only the trivial block over F_2 is needed, which removes the c_mul penalty entirely.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None. This is a constant-factor enabler: B*D^2 is unchanged. Its only route to the B*D^2 << N line is indirect: it makes the UNSAT side of the (4,4..6) cells and the d_F >= 5 population census affordable at larger n and l (memory /n^2 ~ /225-/361 at n=15-19 for C_n; /9 for Z/3; /(3n)^2 stacked), which is where lever 1 (bounded vs growing d_F) is decided. If d_F is bounded by f(m) the subexponential heuristics revive; the enabler itself proves nothing about that.
ideas.prior_art: Faugere-Svartz, 'Groebner bases of ideals invariant under a commutative group: the non-modular case', ISSAC 2013 (hal-00819337; G-degree grading splits Macaulay matrices into |G| blocks of equal size); Steidel, 'Groebner bases of symmetric ideals', JSC 2013 (arXiv:1201.5792); Faugere-Spaenlehauer-Svartz, 'Computing small certificates of inconsistency of quadratic fewnomial systems', ISSAC 2016 (not read; certificates of inconsistency, no group action in the abstract seen); programme: G2 (RESEARCH_IC_NOVEL_DIRECTIONS_20261007 sec G2; research/g2_equivariant_f4_20261008: block ranks at degree <= 3, 128x at n=23, all blocks via DFT over F_{2^d}); ic_next10 item 06 (one equivariant Macaulay pass bit-identical to RREF, 44-73x); Faugere-Gaudry-Huot-Renault 2014 (S_m and 2-torsion by invariant-ring rewriting, not by character blocks). New here: (1) the refutation-only reduction to the trivial block over F_2 (no DFT, no extension field), (2) its application to the certificate census rather than the oracle, (3) the Z/3 stabiliser of the unchained S_4 descent (the chained presentations only have 2-group symmetry), (4) stacking C_n x Z/3 with FGHR.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (searched 2026-10-31 WebSearch: 'Faugere Svartz Groebner bases ideals invariant commutative group non-modular trivial character block Nullstellensatz certificate invariant Macaulay matrix refutation' -> only the 2013 paper, Steidel 2013 and the 2016 fewnomial-certificate paper; no source stating that inconsistency certificates of G-invariant systems live in the trivial isotypic block. In-programme grep of brief/MAP_* and docs: G2 states two blocks are needed; no refutation-only statement found.)

falsifier.design: Arm A (Z/3, unchained S_4; the prototype extended): for n in {11,13,17} and l in {4,5}, draw a random l-dim subspace V of F_{2^n} (polynomial basis arithmetic, K_0 model a2=0,b6=1), pick 8 UNSAT targets x_R (ground truth by 2^{3l} enumeration of S_4(x1,x2,x3,x_R)=0 over V^3), build the n Boolean components of S_4 (resultant formula (a1c2+a2c1)^2+(a1b2+a2b1)(b1c2+b2c1) with a=(x_i+x_j)^2, b=x_i x_j, c=b^2+b6), and for c = 6..3l compute (i) rank and 1-in-rowspace of the full Macaulay matrix (rows m*f_i, deg <= c, squarefree-reduced) and (ii) the same for the orbit-sum matrix under the block 3-cycle; record c*_full, c*_triv, sizes, ranks, wall times. At l=5 (15 vars, C(15,<=10)=30,826 columns) run the full matrix only up to c=8 and the trivial block to closure. Arm B (C_n barrel, free target shift, m=2): n in {5,7}, l=2, window W random, variables s_{i,k} (2n one-hot selectors), w_{ij} (2l window bits), t_j (n target selectors); generators: n components of S_3(x1,x2,x_R) with x_i = sum_k s_{ik} sigma^k(w_i), x_R = sum_j t_j sigma^j(r_0) (Boolean degree 5), one-hot sums and pairwise products. Compute c*_full (python at n=5; msolve -v 2 -g 2 with field equations at n=7, reading the max F4 step degree and the [1] output as the full-system reference) and c*_triv from the orbit-sum matrix under the simultaneous cyclic shift of all selectors (python, both n). Also compute c* of the FIXED-target system over the same orbit-union base for each of the n conjugate targets and record max_j c*_fixed(sigma^j R) for comparison with c*_barrel. Script: extend ideas/symmetry_proto_z3_block.py (Arm A is already implemented).
falsifier.toy_params: Arm A: n=11,13,17; l=4 (12 Boolean unknowns, columns C(12,<=c) <= 4096) and l=5 (15 unknowns); 8 unsat targets per cell; K_0 model y^2+xy=x^3+1 over F_{2^n} with MODS from the script. Arm B: n=5 (3n+2l=19 unknowns) and n=7 (25 unknowns), l=2, m=2, 4 unsat targets (none of the n conjugates decomposes), degrees c <= 7.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: c*_triv = c*_full on 100% of instances in both arms (a theorem; any deviation is a construction bug or a non-invariant presentation). Trivial-block columns = (C(N,<=c) + 2*#fixed monomials)/3 for Z/3 and ~ C(N,<=c)/n for C_n; rank(triv) ~ rank(full)/|G| (at n=7,l=3: 175 vs 509 = 0.344); wall-time ratio at closure >= |G|^2 = 9 (Z/3) and >= n^2 (barrel, dense). For the census content: Arm A gives the first c*(n) readings of the unchained presentation at fixed l (expected c* <= 3l-1 = 11 at l=4, with the lever-1 question being whether c* moves with n at fixed l). Arm B: c*_barrel >= max_j c*_fixed(sigma^j R) with gap 0 or 1 on every instance.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Any instance with c*_triv != c*_full (would contradict the Reynolds argument; indicates the generator span is not G-stable, e.g. because the descent basis is not the same for all summands, which is then the actual finding: the presentation must be built in a common basis). For the enabler claim: if the orbit-sum matrix is no smaller than ~0.6x the full one (orbits mostly of size 1, which cannot happen for prime |G| acting freely on >= 2 variables per block) or if the barrel free-shift closure degree exceeds the fixed-target degree by >= 2 at both n (then the free-shift presentation is the wrong object and the enabler only applies to the Z/3 arm).
falsifier.tools: python3 (numpy uint8 F_2 elimination; ideas/symmetry_proto_z3_block.py), msolve 0.9.5 (-v 2 -g 2, characteristic 2, field equations appended) for the Arm B full-system reference

ideas.risk: The chained presentations the programme actually prices at (4,l) have only 2-group symmetry (see MP-symmetry-5); the C_n barrel is the only odd-order stabiliser available there, and its free-shift system has more unknowns (+n selectors, +1 degree) than the fixed-target system, so the net saving against the fixed-target census must be measured (Arm B), not assumed. Dense-time saving assumes dense elimination; with sparse/structured elimination the gain is smaller.

ideas.title: Isotypic localisation of degree falls and pseudo-solutions: per-character Macaulay deficits (Z/3 over F_4 for binary unchained S_4; S_3 trivial/sign/standard over F_p) and the Specht/Vandermonde containment degree as a lever-1 proof organiser
ideas.statement: For an S_m-symmetric descended Semaev system, the Macaulay row space W_c and the quotient B_{<=c}/W_c are G-modules; in the non-modular case they split into isotypic components and both the rank deficit relative to the semi-regular null (the 'degree fall') and the pseudo-solution space (B_{<=c}/W_c)^* split accordingly. Hypothesis H1: the fall degree and the growth of the last fall degree live in a single isotypic component (trivial for the binary Z/3 action; trivial or sign for S_3 over F_p), so that the lever-1 proof route ('degree-c pseudo-solutions killing W_c but not 1') only needs that block, whose rows/columns are indexed by orbit sums with an n-uniform combinatorial description. Hypothesis H2 (Specht containment): the Vandermonde Delta = prod_{i<j}(x_i - x_j) (the sign-Specht polynomial of shape (1^m)) enters W_c at a degree c_Delta strictly below the closure degree c_1 on unsatisfiable instances, i.e. low-degree pseudo-solutions are forced to the diagonal (repeated summands) before being killed; the gap c_1 - c_Delta measures how much of the solving degree is spent on the diagonal locus that FGHR symmetrisation removes. Binary arm: for Z/3 acting on the unchained S_4 descent, F_2[Z/3] = F_2 x F_4, so rank(full) = rank(triv) + 2 rank(chi) with chi the F_4-character; the nontrivial-block rank is obtained without F_4 arithmetic as (rank_full - rank_triv)/2.
ideas.mechanism: Non-modular representation theory: projectors P_lambda = (dim lambda/|G|) sum_g chi_lambda(g^{-1}) g act on B_{<=c} and commute with multiplication by invariants but NOT with multiplication by arbitrary monomials, so the Macaulay row space is G-stable while individual isotypic pieces are not ideals; still dim W_c = sum_lambda dim P_lambda W_c and 1 in W_c <=> 1 in P_triv W_c, Delta in W_c <=> Delta in P_sign W_c (Delta spans the sign component of the degree-C(m,2) part generated by it). The semi-regular null per block is the isotypic Hilbert series of a generic G-invariant sequence (Breloer-Riener 2026 for S_n; computed here directly by replacing the Semaev components with random G-symmetrised polynomials of the same degrees). The pseudo-solution space is the cokernel; averaging a pseudo-solution with the Reynolds operator keeps phi(1)=1, so there is always a G-invariant pseudo-solution when there is any (trivial block), but the SIZE of the other blocks' cokernels tells whether the obstruction to closure is 'symmetric' (few invariant pseudo-solutions) or 'generic'.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-first-fall-degree-constant (open side: 'whether d_F grows without bound is open; proof route suggested: degree-c pseudo-solutions'); TREAT-summation-cover-monodromy (closes fibre censuses and yield, leaves solving difficulty free); KN-OPEN-8f3d27/-3c8f51. Also positioned against the adjacent_fields.json suggestion 'ideas/isotypic_pseudosolutions' (S_3-isotypic decomposition, test whether the sign component carries the growth) - which this idea subsumes with two added mechanisms.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The closures concern WHAT d_F is (presentation-dependent, unknown growth) and never used representation theory to organise the certificate space; the monodromy closure is about Galois fibres of the summation cover, not about the S_m-module structure of the Macaulay matrix. New mechanisms over the corpus suggestion: (1) the Specht/Vandermonde containment degree c_Delta as a measurable invariant separating 'diagonal' from 'off-diagonal' pseudo-solutions (THM_QUOTIENT_DESCENT1 / FGHR remove the diagonal by invariant-ring rewriting; this measures whether the solver's remaining degrees are spent there); (2) the binary Z/3 instance via rank differences (no F_4 arithmetic), giving the only non-modular isotypic split available over F_2 for a summand-permutation symmetry; (3) per-block semi-regular nulls computed from random G-symmetrised systems.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None directly: theory. It cannot lower B*D^2; it can decide which block a lever-1 proof must address. If H1 holds with the trivial block carrying the fall, then the uniform-in-n pseudo-solution route reduces to functionals on orbit sums (n-independent index set for the barrel, 3-fold smaller for Z/3) - a proof of d_F >= 5 for all n (kills subexponential heuristics) or a bounded f(m) (revives them) would be an exponent-level statement, but it is a consequence of a future proof, not of this experiment.
ideas.prior_art: Moustrou-Riener-Verdure, 'Symmetric ideals, Specht polynomials and solutions to symmetric systems of equations' (arXiv:1912.05266); Breloer-Riener, 'Symmetric and isotypic Hilbert series for symmetric ideals' (arXiv:2606.18895); Debus-Gottwald, Specht ideals for dihedral/type-D reflection groups (arXiv:2506.15335); Gorla-Trebiani, 'Symmetric models for syndrome decoding' (arXiv:2609.14052; proved d_reg of an S_n-symmetric Boolean ideal by Hilbert-function counting); Faugere-Gaudry-Huot-Renault 2014 (invariant-ring rewriting); programme: THM_SEMAEV_FALL1 (attribution of falls to Frobenius/symmetry syzygies), THM_QUOTIENT_DESCENT1 (translation group (Z/2)^{m-1} x| S_m), fpn_degrees.py system_labels (exact degree labels over F_{p^n}). adjacent_fields.json sublane 6 proposes the S_3-isotypic split; the Specht-containment degree and the binary Z/3 rank-difference arm are not in the corpus (grep of MAP_ideas_corpus.json for 'Specht', 'isotypic', 'Vandermonde': 0 cards).
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (no web search; literature lane confirms no programme card uses Specht/isotypic structure; the Specht-containment-degree invariant as a solving-degree diagnostic was not searched)

falsifier.design: Arm P (prime field, S_3 full isotypic): E/F_{p^3} with base {x in F_p}, p in {101, 211, 401, 1009} (p != 2,3 so projectors exist), m=3 unsymmetrised: S_4(x1,x2,x3,x_R) from csd.semaev.S4() specialised to (a,b) over F_{p^3} (fpn_degrees.GF(p,3)); x_i are F_p-scalars so the Weil descent is just the 3 F_p-coordinates of the F_{p^3}-valued polynomial: 3 polynomials in 3 unknowns, total degree <= 12. Append field equations x_i^p - x_i only for the ground truth (solutions = F_p-points); for degree labels use the Macaulay matrix of the 3 polynomials at degrees c = 12..24 (columns C(3+c,3) <= 2925). For 16 unsat and 8 sat targets: per degree, rank of the full matrix and of P_lambda-projected matrices for lambda in {triv, sign, std} (projectors over F_p via the 6 permutation matrices on monomial exponents), compared with the same quantities for a null of random S_3-symmetrised cubic-by-cubic systems of equal degree profile; record c_1 = min{c: 1 in W_c} and c_Delta = min{c : Delta in W_c} (Delta = (x1-x2)(x1-x3)(x2-x3), degree 3), and the dimension of the cokernel per block at c_1 - 1. Arm Z (binary Z/3 via ranks): reuse MP-symmetry-1 Arm A output (n=11,13,17,19,23; l=4; 8 unsat targets): rank_chi(c) = (rank_full(c) - rank_triv(c))/2 per degree, its deficit against the null (random Z/3-symmetrised Boolean sextics with the same number of components), and the cokernel split dim(coker_triv), dim(coker_chi) at c*-1 as a function of n at fixed l.
falsifier.toy_params: Arm P: p = 101, 211, 401, 1009; n=3; m=3; 24 targets per p; degrees c <= 24. Arm Z: n = 11,13,17,19,23; l=4; 8 unsat targets each; c <= 11. Null: 8 random symmetrised draws per cell.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: H1: the rank deficit vs null is confined to one block at the first fall degree (prime arm: >= 90% of the deficit in triv or in sign across all 96 instances, consistently the same block; binary arm: deficit entirely in the trivial block, i.e. rank_chi equals its null to within 1 at every c < c*). H2: c_Delta <= c_1 - 1 on >= 90% of unsat instances with a gap that is constant in p (prime arm) - the diagonal is killed late and separately. Arm Z additionally reports whether c*(n) at l=4 is constant (plateau) or increases over n=11..23 in the unchained presentation.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: Deficits spread across blocks in proportion to block dimension (|deficit_lambda|/dim_lambda equal within 20% across lambda) - the fall is 'generic' and no single-block proof route exists; and/or c_Delta = c_1 on most instances (the sign-Specht polynomial only enters with 1, so pseudo-solutions are never forced to the diagonal first and FGHR's removal of the diagonal is not where the solving degree is spent). Either outcome is recorded; the idea is then an accounting note organising lever 1.
falsifier.tools: python3 (numpy mod-p elimination with p < 2^31; csd.semaev.S4, csd.fpn_degrees.GF/Curve for F_{p^3} arithmetic, sympy for Delta), msolve optional cross-check of c_1 (-v 2 -g 2 over F_p)

ideas.risk: Prime-field arm is at n=3 only (no growth axis in n at toy cost); the binary arm uses the unchained presentation, whose degrees are not the chained D the programme prices (presentation dependence is itself the open issue). Projectors for S_3 need char not 2 or 3, so the full isotypic split is never available on the binary system; only the Z/3 split is.

ideas.title: CRT structure of the group-algebra lift closes N1 and the mu_{2n+1} exponent-shift symmetry: exact lifts are field identity + parity identity + shadow identity, and even-weight summands never lift
ideas.statement: For n in {11, 23, 83, 131} with N = 2n+1 prime and ord_N(2) = n, the redundant representation F_{2^n} = F_2[Z/N]/kernel used by N1 (RESEARCH_IC_NOVEL_DIRECTIONS sec. 3) has F_2[Z/N] = F_2[X]/(X^N-1) = F_2 x F_{2^n} x F_{2^n} (X^N - 1 = (X-1) f(X) f*(X) with f* the reciprocal of f; verified in gp for N = 23, 47, 263). The second F_{2^n} factor is the image under the non-Galois involution iota: X -> X^{-1} (the shadow x-bar = sum_{k in S} gamma^{-k} of x = sum_{k in S} gamma^k), which swaps the two factors because -1 is not in <2> mod N. Consequently the 'exact lift' of S_3(x1,x2,x_R) = 0 to a convolution identity in F_2[Z/N] holds iff three identities hold: (P) the parity identity S_3(|S_1| mod 2, |S_2| mod 2, r(1)) = 0 in F_2, (F) the field identity, (Sh) the shadow identity S_3(x1-bar, x2-bar, r(gamma^{-1})) = 0 in F_{2^n}, where r is the chosen group-algebra lift of x_R. The 132 'extra bits of constraint' of N1 are exactly (P)+(Sh) and are absorbed by the 1+131 bits of freedom in the lift r of the dense target: for odd gamma-weight summands an exact lift exists for about half of the field solutions (whenever x1-bar, x2-bar co-lift to E or both to its twist, which fixes r(gamma^{-1}) up to two values) and carries no information beyond (F); for EVEN gamma-weight summands (the w=2 case specified in N1's own falsifier) the parity identity is S_3(0,0,e) = (0)^2 + 0 + 1 = 1 over F_2 for both e, so the exact-lift count is identically ZERO for a reason unrelated to N1's hypothesis. The exponent shift x -> gamma x (the mu_{2n+1} symmetry of A2) is multiplication by X in F_2[Z/N], acting as (1, gamma, gamma^{-1}) on the three factors: it is a symmetry of the membership set only, never of the curve equation (scaling x is not an isomorphism of y^2+xy=x^3+ax^2+b), so it carries no solver symmetry. N1 is a relabelling of the field problem; the 'additive combinatorics on Z/263' it promised is the field equation in disguise.
ideas.mechanism: Chinese remainder theorem in F_2[X]/(X^N-1) with the factorisation of Phi_N over F_2 into (N-1)/ord_N(2) = 2 irreducibles of degree n; the automorphism X -> X^{-1} of the group algebra permutes the irreducible factors as the coset -<2> does; evaluation of a polynomial identity in a product ring is componentwise. The parity component is S_3 evaluated at (weights mod 2); binary S_3 with b=1 gives S_3(0,0,e) = 1, S_3(0,1,e) = e+1, S_3(1,1,e) = e. The lift freedom of a dense target is the kernel (dimension 1 + n), which surjects onto the parity and shadow components, so (P) and (Sh) can be satisfied by choice of r whenever they are satisfiable at all; satisfiability of (Sh) in r(gamma^{-1}) is the existence of an F_{2^n}-root of the quadratic S_3(x1-bar, x2-bar, Z), i.e. co-lifting of the shadows.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-no-subfield-no-low-degree-membership and TREAT-generic-oracle-bound (the only open door is a non-generic use of the field representation): N1 was the single filed attempt to use the redundant 263-bit representation non-generically. This idea does not go around the wall; it shows N1 never left the field equation, so the door stays as described by the closures. Also disposes of the 'mu_263 exponent-shift symmetry' of A2 (brief sec. 3 item 6 / RESEARCH_IC_NOVEL_DIRECTIONS A2) as a solver symmetry.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: Not applicable in the usual sense: this is a theory closure. ideas.title: Twist-avoiding subspaces at prime degree are the F_2-subspaces on which the inverse-function component Tr(beta/x) is affine: a 2-torsion-invariant Boolean function and the Carlet sum-freedom / Kolomeets component-restriction literature
ideas.statement: For E: y^2 + xy = x^3 + a x^2 + b over F_{2^n}, x != 0 lifts to E(F_{2^n}) iff Tr(x + a + b/x^2) = 0, i.e. iff f(x) := Tr(x) + Tr(beta/x) = Tr(a) with beta = sqrt(b) (Tr(b/x^2) = Tr(beta/x)). A subspace V is twist-avoiding (all-lift: every nonzero x in V lifts to E, none to the twist) iff f is constant on V \ {0}, iff the component function h(x) = Tr(beta/x) of the multiplicative inverse coincides on V \ {0} with the affine function Tr(x) + Tr(a). The function f is invariant under the 2-torsion translation x -> beta/x (x(P+T) = beta/x(P)), so the all-lift property is a property of the orbit of V under this involution and of the 'linear structure' of the inverse function on V. This reformulates open lever 7 (twist-avoiding subspaces at prime degree, toy evidence 0.92x null at N=11, p=2e-5) as a known-type question: for which linear subspaces V of dimension l is a component of x^{-1} affine on V \ {0}? Known results on the inverse function restricted to subspaces (Carlet 2020/1587 and Carlet-Hou 2024/1007 on k-th order sum-freedom; the inverse sums to a nonzero value on every affine subspace not containing 0 and on vector subspaces of dimension k coprime to n in known ranges; Kolomeets on component functions constant on a subspace) suggest that at prime n (no subfields, gcd(l,n)=1 for all l<n) affine restrictions of dimension l >= 3 are exceptional, so all-lift subspaces at cryptographic prime n should be no more frequent than for a random Boolean function of the same weight - closing lever 7 as a structural lever while leaving the (small, constant) exhaustive-search gain at tiny n.
ideas.mechanism: Lifting criterion via the Artin-Schreier trace; Tr(b/x^2) = Tr(sqrt(b)/x) because squaring is a trace-preserving automorphism; translation by the 2-torsion point T = (0, sqrt(b)) acts as x -> beta/x on abscissae (b=1 on K_0: x -> 1/x), preserving f. Hence twist-avoidance = 'Tr(beta x^{-1}) restricted to V is affine' = V is a 'linear structure set' of a component of the inverse. Sum-freedom (sum over V of x^{-1} nonzero) is a weaker, trace-free statement: if Tr(beta/x) were affine on V with dim V >= 2, then sum_{x in V\0} Tr(beta/x) = Tr(beta sum x^{-1}) would equal sum of an affine function = 0 for dim >= 2, giving Tr(beta * sigma_V) = 0 where sigma_V = sum_{x in V\0} x^{-1}; the sum-freedom results constrain sigma_V != 0 and the equality Tr(beta sigma_V) = 0 for ALL beta would force sigma_V = 0 - so the set of beta (curves) admitting a given all-lift V is a hyperplane in beta, which is the quantitative handle: for a fixed V, half of the curves pass the trace test, and the all-lift condition is 2^l - 1 independent-looking trace conditions, matching the random-function null unless x^{-1} has a linear structure on V.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-twist-no-relations ('UNRESOLVED: twist-avoiding factor-base subspaces at prime degree'; brief sec. 3 item 7). Not a bypass of the twist wall (mixed sums never rational, exact); it addresses the one unresolved clause with an external theory instead of a census.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The twist closure's open clause is a question about existence of structured V; the programme's evidence is an exhaustive census at N=11 and a modelled +0.5 bits at composite degree. The reformulation shows the question is about affine restrictions of the inverse function's components on subspaces, where theorems exist (sum-freedom; no linear structures; Charpin-Kyureghyan-style results), and these theorems do not need Frobenius-stability of V (the hypothesis the no-subfield wall needs), so they speak directly to prime n.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None. Twist-avoidance at best doubles the useful base density (+1 bit of relations per summand), a constant; the closures already say so for composite degree. This is a theory/relabelling item whose value is to close lever 7 by citation plus a null-controlled census, or to flag a genuine linear structure of x^{-1} on some V (which would be a new fact about the inverse function, not an ECDLP advance).
ideas.prior_art: Carlet, 'On the properties of the Boolean functions associated to the differential spectrum of general APN functions and their consequences' / 'sum-freedom of the multiplicative inverse function' (ePrint 2020/1587; arXiv:2407.14660 'More on the sum-freedom of the multiplicative inverse function'); Carlet-Hou, ePrint 2024/1007 (k-th order sum-free for small k; cases of k in [4, n-4] coprime to n left open); Kolomeets, component functions constant on a subspace and nonlinearity (mathnet pdma599); Charpin-Kyureghyan, monomial functions with linear structure; programme: TREAT-twist-no-relations (11 Lean theorems for the composite-degree all-lift construction; 0.92x null at N=11); ffd_frobenius_witness.py (Tr-based witness mu = x_R^{-2}).
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (searched 2026-10-31 WebSearch: 'inverse function x^{-1} over F_{2^n} affine on subspaces component function Tr(beta/x) restricted to linear subspace affine dimension bound' -> found the sum-freedom literature (Carlet 2020/1587, Carlet-Hou 2024/1007, arXiv:2407.14660) and Kolomeets' component-constant-on-subspace work; no source stating the exact 'affine component of the inverse on V' criterion for elliptic-curve twist-avoidance. The reformulation itself appears new; the underlying function-theoretic question is studied.)

ideas.title: Modular representation theory of the chained presentation's 2-group symmetry: transfer-image refutation (1 in Tr_G(W_c)) and the Tate-cohomology defect as the first symmetry tool for Z/2 and D_4 over F_2
ideas.statement: The chained Weil-descended systems the programme prices at the decisive cells have only 2-group stabilisers over F_2: the swap x_1 <-> x_2 (Z/2) at m=2 and m=3, and D_4 = <(12),(34),(13)(24)> for the balanced m=4 chain S_3(x1,x2,u), S_3(x3,x4,v), S_3(u,v,x_R) (with u <-> v accompanying the pair swap). Over F_2 these groups are modular: no Reynolds operator, no character blocks, and Faugere-Svartz does not apply - which is why the symmetry inventory has nothing for them. Modular representation theory still gives a one-sided reduction: the transfer Tr_G = sum_g g maps W_c into W_c^G and is computable from orbit sums alone (rows: orbit sums of Macaulay rows; columns: orbit sums of monomials, ~1/|G| each), and 1 in Tr_G(W_c) implies 1 in W_c. The gap W_c^G / Tr_G(W_c) is the Tate cohomology group H^0-hat(G, W_c) (for G = Z/2: the number of trivial summands in the F_2[Z/2]-decomposition W_c = T^a + F^b, equal to a). Hypothesis: on unsatisfiable chained instances the closure certificate lies in the transfer image at the closure degree (c*_Tr = c*_full) on the large majority of instances, so the orbit-sum matrix (memory /|G|^2) decides refutation for 2-group symmetries too; and the defect dimension a_c/dim W_c is small, so most of the Macaulay rank can be computed on orbit representatives even in the modular case.
ideas.mechanism: For a finite group G acting on a vector space M over F_2, Tr_G(M) subset M^G with quotient H^0-hat(G,M); for G = Z/2, F_2[Z/2] = F_2[eps]/(eps^2) with eps = 1+g, indecomposables are the trivial module T and the free module F, Tr(F) = F^G (dim 1), Tr(T) = 0; so dim Tr(W_c) = b (number of free summands) and dim W_c^G = a + b. The closure certificate 1 = sum c_i m_i f_i can be symmetrised: if 1 = Tr(w) for some w in W_c the orbit-sum matrix finds it; if 1 is in W_c^G but not in Tr(W_c) the certificate is 'cohomological' and invisible to orbit sums. Degree falls by Frobenius (THM_SEMAEV_FALL1 Lemma 1) are themselves symmetric under the swap, which suggests W_c is rich in free summands coming from pairs (m f, g(m f)) with m f not invariant; invariant rows m f with m f = g(m f) contribute trivial summands only when their span is not reached by transfers. Measuring a_c, b_c by two F_2 ranks (full matrix restricted to the invariant columns; orbit-sum matrix) is cheap.
ideas.wall_bypassed: TREAT-symmetry-inventory (every tool there is non-modular: FGHR invariant ring, Faugere-Svartz blocks, D_4 invariants over F_p; 'S_4-S_8 symmetrisation unmeasured'); LEAD-ICB-frobenius-search-symmetry ('equivariant elimination is a constant 2-3x vs gf2_elim'); TREAT-first-fall-degree-constant (the (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) cells are unmeasured for memory reasons: 70-357 GB, >250 GB at degree 5).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The inventory's gains are all computed where characters exist in the coefficient field (odd |G| over F_2, or F_p). The 2-group stabilisers of the chained presentation are exactly the case those hypotheses exclude, and the programme recorded them as unusable ('4-torsion/Klein not F_q-valued on subspace bases'; FGHR's symmetriser returns None for m >= 4). Modular representation theory does not need characters; the transfer/fixed-point filtration is the standard replacement and has never been tried on these systems (grep of MAP_closed/MAP_ideas_corpus for 'transfer', 'Tate cohomology', 'modular representation': 0 hits). The memory-bound cells are refutation (UNSAT) measurements, which is the one-sided direction the transfer image provides.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None: engineering enabler for the same cells as MP-symmetry-1, applicable to the presentations actually priced (chained, D_4 at m=4: memory /64 if certificates lie in the transfer image), plus a theory invariant (defect dimension) for the fall-degree attribution. B*D^2 unchanged.
ideas.prior_art: Standard modular representation theory (Alperin, 'Local representation theory'; Benson, 'Representations and cohomology'): transfer, fixed points, Tate cohomology H^0-hat; Faugere-Svartz 2013 explicitly restrict to the non-modular case; Steidel 2013 (symmetric ideals, characteristic 0 / non-modular); programme: FGHR arm B 'specified, never run; native symmetriser returns None for m>=4' (program_self_review.json), equivariant Macaulay oracle (odd C_n only), dreg_closure_m4l6_20261018 (25.8 GB at degree 4; degree 5 needs >250 GB). Use of transfer-image certificates for Boolean Macaulay refutation under 2-group symmetry: not found in the programme; literature not searched.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (no web search; programme grep only)

obstruction_notes_not_filed_as_ideas.note: Over F_q, 0 -> E[phi](F_q) -> E(F_q) -> E'(F_q) -> H^1(Gal, E[phi]) -> H^1(Gal, E) = 0 (Lang) gives E'(F_q)/phi(E(F_q)) = H^1(Z-hat, Z/2) = Z/2 for the 2-isogeny with kernel <T>; the connecting map is a homomorphism to Z/2 (the halving/trace bit). Any filter built from it is homomorphic with 1 bit: closed by LEAD-ICB-cofactor-torsion-quotients and TREAT-wagner-klist; descending through E/<T> is covered by TREAT-transport-conservation (|kappa|^{m-1} = 2^{m-1} exact). No idea.
